focus: Save-time readers, writer and matcher (gaps 1, 5, 6; parse-surface maintainability)
noveltyJustification: 9 of 11 findings were new mechanisms or duplication sites; 2 (the existence of gaps 1 and 5) were partially new because the charter named them without locating their owner.
keyQuestions: How many independent storage-format parsers exist across the five live adapters and five save-time readers, and which can be deleted or merged rather than fixed?
Which of the eight known gaps are worth closing, and what is the smallest change that closes each one?
Which gaps close by removing a surface (an adapter, a sweep, a runtime-matrix row) instead of adding code?
answeredQuestions: How many independent storage-format parsers exist across the five live adapters and five save-time readers, and which can be deleted or merged rather than fixed?
ruledOut: Making the live adapter write a decision record directly
Replacing the matcher scoring with exact text equality

label: No live adapter or sweep writes a decision record; the only writer is a --full-auto save payload carrying operatorDecisions through the normalizer and the per-packet save pipeline, which is gap 1 exactly.

The Claude Stop hook already spawns a context autosave through generate-context.js and its payload carries no operatorDecisions, so gap 1's smallest Claude fix is attaching pending queue records to an autosave that already runs.
Gap 5 is a prose contract, not a detection gap: the detector already emits keyed candidates and the save instruction asks the model to decide whether each reply clearly answers its question.

Gap 6 is one executable filter plus one prose restatement: isProcessQuestion runs at capture and on chat candidates while the save instruction repeats the exclusion in prose, and only the code copy is testable.

The parse surface is five store readers each owning its own sessionIdOf and chatTurnsOf plus record mapping; Codex and Pi hold four identically named functions with different bodies, the clearest merge candidate.
The shared pairing detector already works: every sweep calls chatCandidatesFromTurns from chat-questions.mjs, so only turn extraction is duplicated across the five stores.

The queue row schema is declared twice in two languages (an object literal in capture-core and a TypeScript DecisionQueueRecord interface in the matcher CLI), so a new field is invisible to the save consumer until both are edited.

The consumed log has three implementations: capture-core reads it, the writer reads and appends it, and the matcher CLI declares its own filename, path builder and reader while reusing only the writer's append.

The table matcher is a second silent adjudicator: its answer gate and weighted score (threshold 0.4 plus tie margin) consume a key without the model seeing the pairing rationale, and nothing enforces that the model ran it.
Sweep selection is prose, not detection: the save instruction branches on runtime name and names five scripts, so a sixth runtime adds a sixth prose branch and a sixth reader with no shared resolver.

Gap 8 has a save-time consequence: the instruction tells the model the Codex and Pi sweeps print nothing when both lists are empty, and an unreadable transcript now produces the same silence, so a clean run is indistinguishable from a failed read.

direction: Making the live adapter write a decision record directly
reason: A capture hook runs before a bound packet exists and before the operator agrees the decided sentence, so it would guess the packet or write an unbound row.

direction: Replacing the matcher scoring with exact text equality
reason: The scorer exists because hand-written rows phrase the same decision differently; exact equality regresses the case it was built for.
